headline: Sellers Run the Board as Energy Holds Alone; American Eagle Craters Mid-Session
body_html:
Thursday's session has turned decisively defensive, with declining issues outnumbering advancers by more than three to one — 414 names lower against just 126 in positive territory across the 545-stock universe. The damage is broad: Semiconductors lead the retreat with a mid-session loss of 2.4%, followed by Homebuilders off 1.84% and Materials down 1.46%. Industrials and Consumer names are also nursing losses above one percent, leaving Energy as the sole sector in the green, clinging to a 0.5% gain on the back of surging crude prices.

Oil's move is the dominant story of the day. Crude has surged to $105 a barrel after an escalation of tanker attacks in the Middle East, compounded by Houthi forces seizing a strategically critical Red Sea port. The dual threat to global energy supply lines has lit a fire under oil-linked equities: Chord Energy is among the session's top performers, advancing 2.39%. National HealthCare leads all gainers at 2.84%, while Chemed Corp. adds 2.22%, giving healthcare services a rare bright spot amid the sector's broader 0.81% decline.

The session's standout mover on the downside is American Eagle Outfitters, which has plunged 15.38% mid-session, dragging consumer-apparel sentiment lower. Boot Barn is off 6.28%, while BHP Group and Century Aluminum have extended the punishment in Materials. Into the close, watch whether rising Treasury yields — ahead of wholesale inflation data — continue to weigh on rate-sensitive sectors, and whether oil's geopolitical premium holds.

briefs.headline: Oil Rockets to $105 on Red Sea Escalation
briefs.body: Crude oil has surged to $105 a barrel after a fresh wave of tanker attacks in the Middle East and reports that Houthi forces have seized a key Yemeni Red Sea port. The twin developments have rattled global energy supply chains and driven a sharp bid for oil-linked equities, making Energy the only sector in positive territory Thursday.

briefs.headline: American Eagle Skids 15% in Heaviest Single-Stock Selling
briefs.body: American Eagle Outfitters is the session's most dramatic casualty, shedding 15.38% mid-session and anchoring a broader slide in consumer-apparel names. Boot Barn is also under significant pressure, off 6.28%, reflecting deteriorating sentiment across discretionary retail as investors grow cautious on the consumer spending outlook.

briefs.headline: Treasury Yields Climb Ahead of Wholesale Inflation Print
briefs.body: Government bond yields are drifting higher as markets position for a closely watched wholesale inflation report expected later this week. The move adds a headwind to rate-sensitive sectors including Homebuilders, which are nursing mid-session losses of 1.84%, and reinforces a cautious tone across growth-oriented equities.

briefs.headline: Macy's Turnaround Narrative Strengthens After Strong Quarter
briefs.body: Macy's delivered results that beat expectations and prompted management to raise its forward guidance, signaling that the retailer's restructuring efforts are beginning to produce tangible results. The report stands as a rare positive data point in an otherwise difficult day for the broader consumer sector.

briefs.headline: Semiconductors Pace Sector Declines at -2.4%
briefs.body: The semiconductor complex is Thursday's hardest-hit sector, shedding 2.4% at midday, with Entegris among the more visible losers, declining 4.86%. Weakness in chip-related names is compounding the day's negative breadth and underscoring investor caution toward technology hardware amid uncertain demand signals.

briefs.headline: BRICS Summit Convenes as Gulf Tensions Test Bloc Cohesion
briefs.body: India is hosting a BRICS summit against a backdrop of rising tensions stemming from the ongoing Iran conflict, which observers say is straining unity within the multi-nation group. Separately, Algeria severed diplomatic ties with the UAE, adding another layer of geopolitical friction across a region already roiled by escalating energy-supply risks.
